summary: Nine machines are scheduled for repair over the next 10 days, with a total expected cost of $85,444. Three machines are left unplanned because their forecasted remaining life is well beyond the planning windowcars. Repairs are scheduled on days with available technicians, avoiding the no-technician days. The plan prioritizes machines with higher failure risk or full sensor wear.

reasons.0: Pressure sensor is at 100% wear and has a 10% chance of failing before repair. Scheduled on day 2 to address the risk promptly.
reasons.1: Vibration sensor wear is 62% and forecasted life is 5-14 days. Scheduled on day 3 to prevent potential failure.
reasons.4: Pressure sensor is at 100% wear, though failure chance is 0%. Scheduled on day 7 to replace worn sensor.
reasons.5: Noise sensor wear is 64% and forecasted life is 14-35 days. Scheduled on day 10 to maintain reliability.
reasons.6: Pressure sensor is at 100% wear, though failure chance is 0%. Scheduled on day 9 to replace worn sensor.
reasons.7: Current sensor wear is 83% with a 28% chance of failing before repair. Scheduled on day 8 to mitigate high risk.
reasons.9: Noise sensor wear is 88% and forecasted life is 7-18 days. Scheduled on day 4 to avoid failure.
reasons.10: Temperature sensor wear is 93% and forecasted life is only 1-4 days. Scheduled on day 1 to prevent imminent failure.
reasons.11: Pressure sensor is at 100% wear and forecasted life is 0-7 days. Scheduled on day 0 for immediate repair.

steps: Inspect pressure lines, fittings and seals for leaks or cracking.
Replace worn seals and damaged hose sections.
Check the pressure relief valve operates freely.
Function test before restart.
safety_steps: Apply lockout/tagout to the machine's main power isolator and keep the key with the technician.
Isolate all stored energy (electrical, pressure, spring) and verify zero energy before opening any guard.
Wear protective equipment: safety glasses, gloves and hearing protection.
